cluster_name: ICE arrests British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos for deportation
tldr: The headline layer presents this story with near-total uniformity as a law-enforcement action — ICE detaining and deporting a British far-right figure — with no outlet offering any editorial defence of Yiannopoulos across twelve titles. The only meaningful divergences are label choices: outlets split between 'far-right', 'right-wing', 'conservative', and 'provocateur'; RT alone wraps 'illegal alien' in scare quotes; and The Independent alone names the enforcement arm as 'Trump's ICE', the sole headline to attach the arrest to a political principal rather than a neutral institution.
event_summary: ICE arrested British commentator Milo Yiannopoulos at New Orleans International Airport on August 27 after he overstayed his US visa; an immigration judge had issued a final removal order on July 22 when he failed to appear. He is held pending deportation to the United Kingdom.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to label Yiannopoulos 'Conservative' rather than 'far-right' or 'provocateur', and the only one to place 'illegal alien' in scare quotes — signalling distance from DHS framing without explicitly contesting the arrest.

The only headline to frame the detention as 'Trump's ICE' rather than a neutral institutional act, and the only one to foreground personal humiliation ('looks dejected in mugshot') — a tabloid register absent from all other titles.
Headlines Yiannopoulos as 'Disgraced Provocateur' — the sharpest editorial distancing in the corpus, and notably from a fellow conservative American publication rather than a left-leaning outlet.

Only headline to lead with the specific legal cause (overstaying visa) and state the deportation destination — 'Will Be Deported to United Kingdom' — foregrounding procedural finality where other outlets stop at the detention fact.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, twelve outlets across nine countries unanimously frame the story as routine immigration enforcement — an ICE arrest and impending deportation — with divergence limited to how Yiannopoulos is politically labeled and whether 'Trump's ICE' or a neutral institution is credited for the action.
